title: When Has a Bayesian Neural Network Sampled Enough? Adaptive Inference Time with Statistical Guarantees
abstract: arXiv:2610.12212v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bayesian neural network predictions are commonly approximated using a fixed number of Monte Carlo samples per input, without controlling the resulting error that comes from this finite sample. We propose the use of confidence sequences to dynamically determine how many samples are needed while maintaining statistical guarantees. We consider several ways in which predictive probabilities are used, including identifying the most likely class, approximating the full predictive distribution, and resolving probability-threshold decisions. Sampling stops once the corresponding decision can be made with the desired guarantee. Experiments show that the method allocates the computational budget efficiently, assigning more samples to ambiguous inputs than to easy inputs while preserving reliable decisions and reducing overall latency relative to a fixed Monte Carlo budget.

translated_title: 贝叶斯神经网络何时采样足够？具有统计保证的自适应推理时间
translated_abstract: 贝叶斯神经网络的预测通常使用每个输入固定数量的蒙特卡洛样本来近似，而无法控制这种有限采样所带来的误差。我们提出使用置信序列来动态确定所需样本数量，同时保持统计保证。我们考虑了几种使用预测概率的方式，包括识别最可能的类别、近似完整的预测分布，以及解决概率阈值决策问题。一旦能够以期望的保证做出相应决策，采样即停止。实验表明，该方法能够高效分配计算预算，为模糊输入分配比简单输入更多的样本，在保持可靠决策的同时，相对于固定蒙特卡洛预算降低了总体延迟。
tldr: 该论文提出使用置信序列动态确定贝叶斯神经网络的蒙特卡洛采样数量，根据输入难度自适应分配计算预算，在提供统计保证的同时显著降低推理延迟。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes using confidence sequences to adaptively determine the number of Monte Carlo samples needed for Bayesian neural network inference, efficiently allocating computational budget based on input difficulty while maintaining statistical guarantees and reducing overall latency.
